sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Cell** is the fundamental, structural, and functional unit of all living organisms.
First discovered in **1665** by **Robert Hooke** using a primitive microscope.
Present in all living organisms, forming unicellular (amoeba) and multicellular (humans, plants) bodies.
It is the core basis of life, metabolism, heredity, and physiological activities in biology.
High-scoring static General Science section covering direct one-liners on organelles, inventors, and cell division.
The study of cells is called **Cytology**. The largest cell is the **ostrich egg**; the smallest is **Mycoplasma**.

items.title: Introduction and Discovery of Cell
items.content:
• Term 'Cell' derived from Latin word **'Cellula'** meaning a small room.
• **Robert Hooke** observed dead cork cells and coined the term in his book **Micrographia** (1665).
• **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek** (1674) first observed **living cells** like bacteria, protozoa, and RBCs.
• **Mnemonic for Discoverers:** **'Hooke caught dead, Leeuwenhoek found living'** (Hooke = dead cork cells, Leeuwenhoek = living cells).

items.title: Cell Theory and Modern Additions
items.content:
• Formulated by German botanist **M.J. Schleiden** (1838) and zoologist **Theodor Schwann** (1839).
• **Core Postulates:** All living things are made of cells; cell is the basic unit of life.
• **Rudolf Virchow** (1855) added **'Omnis cellula e cellula'** meaning all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
• Viruses are an **exception** to cell theory as they lack cellular machinery.

items.title: Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic Cells
items.content:
• **Prokaryotic Cells:** Primitive cells, lacking a true membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (e.g., **Bacteria**, **Cyanobacteria**, **Mycoplasma**).
• **Eukaryotic Cells:** Advanced cells with a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (e.g., **Plant cells**, **Animal cells**, **Fungi**).
• **Ribosomes:** 70S type in prokaryotes, 80S type (and 70S in mitochondria/chloroplast) in eukaryotes.

items.title: Major Cell Organelles and Functions
items.content:
• **Mitochondria:** Known as the **'Powerhouse of the Cell'**; produces **ATP** via cellular respiration.
• **Ribosomes:** Known as **'Protein Factories'**; sites of protein synthesis.
• **Lysosomes:** Known as **'Suicide Bags of the Cell'**; contain hydrolytic digestive enzymes.
• **Golgi Apparatus:** Known as the **'Traffic Police of the Cell'**; packaging and dispatching molecules.
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):** Rough ER (has ribosomes for protein) and Smooth ER (lipid synthesis and detoxification).

items.title: Plant Cell vs Animal Cell Differences
items.content:
• **Cell Wall:** Present in plant cells (made of **cellulose**); completely absent in animal cells.
• **Plastids:** Present in plant cells (**Chloroplast**, **Chromoplast**, **Leucoplast**); absent in animal cells.
• **Vacuoles:** Large central permanent vacuole in plant cells; small, temporary vacuoles in animal cells.
• **Centrosome/Centrioles:** Present in animal cells for cell division; absent in most higher plant cells.

items.title: Cell Division: Mitosis and Meiosis
items.content:
• **Mitosis:** Equational division; occurs in **somatic cells** for growth, repair, and regeneration; produces **2 diploid (2n)** daughter cells.
• **Meiosis:** Reductional division; occurs in **germ cells** for gamete formation (sperm and egg); produces **4 haploid (n)** daughter cells.
• **Mnemonic for Cell Cycle Phases:** **'I P-MAT on the floor'** (Interphase, Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase).

items.definition: Remember **'Mighty Mitochondria'** — Mighty sounds like Mitochondria, and it is the mighty powerhouse that makes ATP currency.
Remember **'Lysol'** (the cleaning agent) — Lysosomes clean up the cell waste, but if they burst, they destroy the whole cell ('suicide bags').
Use the acronym **IPMAT** for cell cycle stages: **I**nterphase, **P**rophase, **M**etaphase, **A**naphase, **T**elophase.
Remember **'CPW'** (Chloroplast, Plastid, Wall) — Plant cells exclusively have Chloroplast, Plastids, and a rigid Cell Wall.
Associate **'Brown Nut'** — Robert Brown discovered the **Nut**cleus (Nucleus) in 1831.
Think of **'Post Office'** — Golgi apparatus collects, packages, and ships proteins like a postal service.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Dead and Living Cell Discoverers
items.definition: Students often confuse Robert Hooke with Antonie van Leeuwenhoek. **Robert Hooke** discovered dead cork cells, whereas **Leeuwenhoek** discovered living cells.
Students confuse plant cell wall with bacterial or fungal cell walls. Plant cell walls are made of **cellulose**, fungal cell walls of **chitin**, and bacterial cell walls of **peptidoglycan**.
Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles, but they **do contain ribosomes** (70S type floating in cytoplasm). Never say prokaryotes have zero organelle-like structures.

items.term: Mistake 4: Function of Mitosis vs Meiosis
items.definition: Mitosis is for **growth and repair** in somatic cells, while Meiosis is strictly for **gamete formation** and sexual reproduction. Do not mix up their occurrence sites.
Cytoplasm is the jelly inside the cell excluding the nucleus, whereas **Protoplasm** includes both cytoplasm and nucleoplasm (coined by Purkinje).

items.term: Mistake 6: Powerhouse of the Cell Misconception
items.definition: Only eukaryotes have mitochondria. Prokaryotes generate ATP across their cell membranes (mesosomes), not via true mitochondria.
The structural and functional unit of life, capable of independent existence and performing all life processes.
**Robert Hooke** (1665) discovered cells in cork; **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek** (1674) discovered living cells.
Proposed by **Schleiden and Schwann**; later expanded by **Rudolf Virchow** with the biogenesis law.
Discovered by **Robert Brown** (1831); contains genetic material (**DNA/RNA**) and directs all metabolic reactions.
Site of aerobic respiration and synthesis of **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate), known as the powerhouse.
Discovered by **George Palade**; responsible for protein synthesis, termed protein factories.
Contain powerful digestive enzymes capable of autolysis (suicide bags of the cell).
Include **Chloroplasts** (photosynthesis), **Chromoplasts** (colors), and **Leucoplasts** (food storage).
Provides rigidity and mechanical support exclusively in plant cells, fungi, and bacteria; absent in animals.
Results in **2 identical diploid** daughter cells used for body growth and tissue repair.
Results in **4 genetically distinct haploid** cells essential for sexual reproduction and genetic diversity.
The specialized branch of biology dedicated to the detailed study of cell structure, function, and chemistry.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks direct matching questions on organelle names (e.g., Powerhouse, Suicide Bags, Protein Factory) and their discoverers. Memorize the data tables thoroughly.
Focus heavily on the difference between plant and animal cells, especially cell wall composition and plastid types, as these are staple MCQ topics in UP PET exam.
Watch out for trick questions regarding prokaryotic ribosomes. Even though prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles, 70S ribosomes are freely present in their cytoplasm.
Do not confuse the discoverer of the cell (Robert Hooke) with the discoverer of the nucleus (Robert Brown). Both are popular options designed to confuse aspirants.

keyTakeaways: Cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665.
Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell producing ATP, discovered by Altman.
Plant cells possess a rigid cellulose cell wall and plastids, which are absent in animal cells.
Ribosomes (Palade particles) are the protein factories of the cell.
Mitosis occurs in somatic cells for growth, while Meiosis occurs in germ cells for gamete formation.
Rudolf Virchow gave the famous maxim 'Omnis cellula e cellula' supporting cell lineage.
